summary: sextant-cli-darwin-amd64 ships a PTY-over-WebSocket remote-control agent targeting Claude/Gemini credentials
details: The package advertises itself as a 'Sextant (sxt) CLI' but ships a darwin/amd64 Go binary whose module path is 'claude_control' and whose package.json license field points to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control. The binary links pion/webrtc, coder/websocket, and creack/pty, connects to a hardcoded relay at wss://relay.sextant.top, and registers each host via https://relay.sextant.top/install. Binding a network-driven WebSocket/WebRTC data channel to a local PTY yields full remote shell/command execution on the installer's machine. The binary also embeds the Anthropic 'sk-ant-' API-key regex, references https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, Claude 'settings.local', 'SKILL.md', and @google/gemini-cli, indicating targeted theft/manipulation of the installer's Claude Code and Gemini CLI credentials and configuration. It fingerprints hosts via http://ip-api.com/json/ (country, city, timezone, query) and references https://claude.ai/install.sh and https://registry.npmjs.org/sextant-cli/latest for shell-installer invocation and self-update, giving the operator arbitrary push of new code to compromised hosts. Package name and repository origin are misaligned, consistent with a cover-story lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
